headline: Interaction structure and forcing set stability and amplification in multispecies systems
label: Species Interaction Dynamics Modeling
summary: Stability and amplification measures on interaction structure are now paired with learned parameter inference from spatial patterns.
synthesis: The common thread is how interaction structure and external forcing determine the dynamical state of multispecies systems. A spatial reaction-diffusion model places competing species under climate, pollution and cooperation, with a Swin Transformer inferring its parameters from two snapshots. A stochastic logistic model with random interaction-network ensembles uses dynamical mean-field theory to map stability phases, relating microbiome association diversity to proximity to the edge of instability. A published study applies the H2-norm to empirical networks, reporting that food webs, signaling pathways and gene regulatory circuits favor signal passing. The three items are methodologically distinct and overlap only partly in scope. What is new is the explicit use of stability and amplification measures on interaction structure, alongside learned parameter inference from pattern data in the spatial case.
